public_rationale: Salesforce publicly connected AI productivity gains to reduced hiring plans. That is relevant evidence of labor substitution, but does not show AI independently replacing an engineer's responsibilities. SWE-Lancer documents capability limits, not their effect on employment. Neither source settles the combined absence-of-proof and causal claim.
limitations: The result depends on distinguishing full-role replacement from partial automation and avoided hiring.
Later deployments cannot establish that replacement had already occurred when the post appeared.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is still no tangible proof that AI is replacing software engineers because AI can't replace them.

statement.excerpt: This is, by the way, why we are still yet to get any tangible proof that AI is replacing software engineers…because it can’t.

from_speaker: still yet to get any tangible proof
our_interpretation: Assess the public evidence and capabilities existing by September 29, 2025, rather than treating the sentence as an unlimited forecast.
In context, replacement means taking over an engineer's substantive responsibilities sufficiently to replace a position. Generating some code does not establish this.
Reduced hiring through human productivity gains is relevant counterevidence, but differs from independently performing the full role.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence must establish both the absence of documented replacement and that a demonstrated capability limitation explains that absence. Failed searches or isolated benchmark failures alone are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented deployment must show AI taking over substantive engineering responsibilities and replacing positions by the post date, or directly disprove the claimed causal explanation.

evidence.locator: Page 15, Marc Benioff's discussion of engineering efficiency
evidence.publisher: Salesforce; transcript by S&P Global Market Intelligence
evidence.explanation: The company linked greater engineering productivity to a hiring freeze. This challenges a broad assertion that AI cannot substitute for engineering labor, but does not document autonomous replacement of existing engineers.

SWE-Lancer documents substantial limitations on real freelance engineering tasks. It neither measures employment replacement nor establishes that technical incapacity caused an absence of replacement.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated deployment and staffing records showing whether AI took over engineering responsibilities before September 29, 2025, together with evidence identifying why replacement did or did not occur.
